'''Rachel Angharad Oliver''' is a Professor of [[Materials Science]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] and a fellow of [[Robinson College, Cambridge]]. She works on characterisation techniques for [[gallium nitride]] materials for dark-emitting diodes and laser diodes.<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref name=ORCID>{{EuropePMC}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Oliver studied engineering and materials science at the [[University of Oxford]] and completed an industrial placement in metallurgy.{{when|date=September 2018}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=Structuring a Career Around Gallium Nitride|date=2010 |publisher=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|journal=Science|access-date=2018-09-29|language=en|doi=10.1126/science.caredit.a1000032|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/structuring-career-around-gallium-nitride|first=Elisabeth|last=Pain|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Her final year masters project was in optoelectronic materials.<ref name=":0" /> She completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree at the [[University of Oxford]] in 2003,<ref name=raodphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015712442|title=Growth and characterisation of nitride nanostructures|first=Rachel Angharad|last=Oliver|date=2003|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.400219}}|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=59185823|archive-date=9 December 2019|access-date=30 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209060023/http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015712442|url-status=dead}}</ref> where she began to work with [[gallium nitride]] under the supervision of [[Andrew Briggs]].<ref name=":0" /> She used [[metalorganic vapour-phase epitaxy]] (MOVPE) to grow [[quantum dot]]s.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career==
She joined the [[University of Cambridge]] in 2003 as a [[Royal Commission for the Exhibition of 1851]] [[postdoctoral]] [[research fellow]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2006 Oliver was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] (URF) at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/rachel-oliver-7819/|location=London|title=Dr Rachel Oliver: Research Fellow|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|author=Anon|year=2018|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-09-29|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930033726/https://royalsociety.org/people/rachel-oliver-7819/|archivedate=2018-09-30}}</ref> She studied the morphology of [[gallium nitride]] [[light-emitting diode]]s (LEDs), identifying what factors controlled their efficiency and the impact of defects.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] (EPSRC) grant to study semi-polar nitride based structures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gtr.ukri.org/projects?ref=EP%2FJ003603%2F1|title=Study of semi-polar and non-polar nitride based structures for opto-electronic device applications|last=Oliver|first=Rachel|website=ukri.og|year=2019|access-date=2018-09-29|publisher=UK Research and Innovation}}</ref>

She was appointed a lecturer at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 2011.<ref name=notman>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/careers/the-mothers-of-invention/8303.article|title=The mothers of invention: Nina Notman profiles four researchers successfully balancing an academic career with family life|year=2015|first=Nina|last=Notman|publisher=[[Chemistry World]]|website=chemistryworld.com|access-date=2018-09-29|language=en|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820102111/https://www.chemistryworld.com/careers/the-mothers-of-invention/8303.article|archivedate=2020-08-20}}</ref> Oliver studies [[gallium nitride]] materials for [[Light-emitting diode|LEDs]] and [[laser diode]]s.<ref name=scopus/><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.msm.cam.ac.uk/people/oliver|title=Rachel Oliver|last=Wineman|first=Adina|date=2016-08-09|website=msm.cam.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-09-29}}</ref> Her research considers ways to engineer the nanostructure of light emitting diodes and how this impacts macroscopic device performance.<ref name=":2" /> She has developed [[Atom-Probe Tomography|atom-probe tomography]] and [[scanning capacitance microscopy]] to study nitride devices.<ref name=":2" />

Oliver is also working on single-photon [[indium gallium nitride]] quantum dots for quantum crystallography.<ref name=":2" /> She has looked at the impact of threading dislocations on the quality factor of InGaN cavities. Her group developed the first blue-emitting single-photon source.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ses.ac.uk/2016/01/05/collaboration-casts-new-light-on-quantum-dots/|title=Collaboration Casts New Light On Quantum Dots - Science and Engineering|publisher=Science and Engineering|website=ses.ac.uk|year=2016|author=Anon|access-date=2018-09-29|language=en-GB}}</ref> She was the first to note [[rabi oscillation]]s of GaN quantum dots.{{cn|date=November 2023}} She designed a quasi-two-temperature growth method to pattern GaN quantum dots, which improved their emission by a factor of ten.<ref name=":3" />

===Awards and honours===
Oliver was elected a [[Fellow of the Institute of Materials, Minerals and Mining]] (FIMMM) in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|last=IOM3|title=IOM3 members recognised in Women's Engineering Society's Top 50 Women in Engineering: Sustainability|url=https://www.iom3.org/resource/iom3-members-recognised-in-women-s-engineering-society-s-top-50-women-in-engineering--sustainability.html|access-date=2021-04-07|website=www.iom3.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Cambridge Centre for Gallium Nitride|date=2019-03-26|title=Rachel elected to Fellowship of IOM3|url=https://www.gan.msm.cam.ac.uk/news/rachel-elected-to-fellowship-of-iom3|access-date=2021-04-07|website=www.gan.msm.cam.ac.uk|language=en}}</ref> She held a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] from 2006 to 2011.<ref name=:1/> In 2021 she was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Academy celebrates first new Fellows elected under Fit for the Future diversity initiative |url=https://www.raeng.org.uk/news/news-releases/2021/september/academy-celebrates-first-new-fellows-elected-under |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |access-date=23 September 2021 |archive-date=22 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210922161438/https://www.raeng.org.uk/news/news-releases/2021/september/academy-celebrates-first-new-fellows-elected-under |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in 2023 was awarded the academy's Chair in Emerging Technologies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Rachel Oliver |url=https://raeng.org.uk/ciet-rachel-oliver |access-date=2024-03-12 |website=Royal Academy of Engineering |language=en}}</ref>

She was awarded an [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] for her services to Materials Engineering  in the [[2025 New Year Honours|2025 King's New Years Honours List.]]

==Personal life==
Oliver's husband is a [[cardiology|cardiologist]] with whom she has a son.<ref name=notman/>
